department: Department of Chemical, Biological, and Bioengineering

deadline.value: General Fall priority admission and merit-based funding deadline is January 15 (applied automatically with the admission application); general international Fall deadline is May 15.
deadline.quote: Priority Admission Application Deadline / Priority Funding Deadline (applies only to Fall semester admissions): January 15 | International Student Admission Application Deadline: May 15

gre_general.value: GRE scores are not required for the Bioengineering Ph.D. program.

gre_subject.value: ETS does not offer a GRE Subject Test in Bioengineering or Biomedical Engineering.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: The Bioengineering Ph.D. admissions page does not state whether a pre-admission faculty supervisor commitment is required.

funding.value: Engineering Ph.D. students compete for College of Engineering GRAs (dependent on faculty grant funding), GTAs, and Graduate College Doctoral GTAs ($20,000 minimum 9-month stipend plus tuition and health insurance).
funding.quote: Graduate Research Assistantships (GRAs) are available to M.S. and Ph.D. students. ... Availability of GRAs is dependent on faculty research areas and funding/grant status. | Academic background and familiarity with course content will play a role in selection for GTA positions.

also.quote: However, currently only a portion of qualified students will be supported as GTAs.

entry_route.value: Applicants may enter directly with a bachelor's degree (3.5 minimum GPA) or with a prior master's degree (3.0 minimum GPA) in Bioengineering, Biomedical Engineering, or a closely related field.
entry_route.quote: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Bioengineering, Biomedical Engineering, or a closely related engineering or science discipline, with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (for students with a prior Master's degree) or a minimum GPA of 3.5 (for students without a prior Master's degree).

notes: Offers two Ph.D. tracks: (1) Neurotechnology and Neural Engineering, and (2) Molecular, Cellular, and Systems Engineering.
